about_blocks.text: Into Action Recovery 100 Ave is a residential house for men in recovery from alcohol and drug addiction, at 12991 100 Avenue in north Surrey, BC. Into Action Recovery Society opened its first program in 2012 and now runs three houses in Surrey, one in Burnaby and one in Abbotsford, plus sober living in Vancouver.
about_blocks.html: Into Action Recovery 100 Ave is a residential house for men in recovery from alcohol and drug addiction, at 12991 100 Avenue in north Surrey, BC. Into Action Recovery Society opened its first program in 2012 and now runs three houses in Surrey, one in Burnaby and one in Abbotsford, plus sober living in Vancouver.

about_blocks.text: From the street, 100 Ave is a large white house set back behind a lawn and a wide driveway, with tall trees around it and a passenger van in the driveway in the centre's photo. The photos Into Action has published show plain, tidy bedrooms: a single room with a queen bed and dresser, and a shared room with two beds and big windows.

about_blocks.text: A weekday here follows a fixed timetable. Men start with a morning check-in, then move through one-to-one counselling, group therapy and a fitness session, and finish with a recovery meeting in the evening. Groups cover addiction education, coping skills, relapse prevention and the Twelve Steps, using ideas from CBT, DBT and SMART Recovery. Staff also take the house to community meetings, on walks and hikes, and out for groceries.

about_blocks.text: The program at 100 Ave is Into Action's First Stage. The centre sets a 60-day minimum and extends stays case by case; recovery.com lists 30 to 90 days. Into Action is clear that it is not a medical or mental health facility. There are no nurses or doctors on site, so detox has to be done first, and residents use a partnered virtual clinic or their own physician.

about_blocks.text: It is a private program. recovery.com puts the likely cost at $10,000 to $30,000 CAD, and Into Action says it can usually admit a man within days of the first call. The call is confidential, and the intake team will also say whether 100 Ave or another of its houses has the right bed open.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Into Action Recovery 100 Ave

faqs.question: What does a day look like at Into Action Recovery 100 Ave?

answer_blocks.text: It runs to a set schedule from morning to evening. Men begin with a check-in, then attend one-to-one counselling, group therapy and physical fitness, and end the day at a recovery meeting. Downtime is kept short on purpose, because Into Action says idle hours are when cravings take over.

Downtime is kept short on purpose, because Into Action says idle hours are when cravings take over.

faqs.question: How much does the 100 Ave house cost?

answer_blocks.text: recovery.com estimates $10,000 to $30,000 CAD, depending on length of stay. Into Action is private pay and gives a full breakdown on the first call rather than publishing prices online.

faqs.question: How long do men stay at 100 Ave?

answer_blocks.text: Usually 60 days or longer. Into Action's First Stage has a 60-day minimum with extensions, its other pages mention 30, 60 and 90-day options, and recovery.com lists 30 to 90 days. Into Action says most men do better with 60 days or more.

faqs.question: Do I need to detox before coming to 100 Ave?

answer_blocks.text: Yes, if you need medical withdrawal management. The house has no medical staff, so detox happens at another facility first. Into Action's intake team says it can help book detox so you move straight into the house afterwards.

answer_blocks.text: It is at 12991 100 Avenue in north Surrey, a few minutes by car from Surrey Central and the city centre around King George Boulevard. Downtown Vancouver is roughly 35 minutes away over the Pattullo Bridge, and New Westminster and Burnaby are 15 to 25 minutes away.

faqs.question: What therapies are used at 100 Ave?

answer_blocks.text: Group therapy and one-to-one counselling are the core. recovery.com lists CBT, DBT, trauma-focused therapy, relapse prevention and 12-step facilitation for the Surrey houses, and Into Action's own FAQ adds SMART Recovery and wellness groups.

faqs.question: Does 100 Ave treat anxiety or depression?

answer_blocks.text: Not directly. Into Action says it is not a mental health facility and focuses on stopping substance use. It supports whatever mental health plan a resident already has with his own care team, including medication.

faqs.question: How do families stay in touch?

answer_blocks.text: Contact starts after the first restriction period and goes as far as the resident wants. Into Action encourages family involvement, and once restrictions lift a resident can ask for a weekend pass.

faqs.question: Is 100 Ave the same as Into Action's other Surrey houses?

answer_blocks.text: The program is the same. Into Action says all three Surrey houses run the same treatment model; they differ in the building and the neighbourhood. The other two are on 87B Avenue in Newton (Bear Creek) and on 113B Avenue.
